# Component: the CLI and `seahaven check`

Modules: `seahaven/cli/` (`__init__.py`, `new.py`, `check.py`, `docs.py`, `fixture.py`, `serve.py`,
`templates/`) and `seahaven/lint/` (`__init__.py`, `ddl.py`, `code.py`, `coverage.py`,
`fixtures.py`). Standard library `argparse`; no CLI framework.

## 1. Entry point and world discovery

`[project.scripts] seahaven = "seahaven.cli:main"`. Subcommands: `new`, `check`, `docs`, `fixture`
(`list`, `freeze`, `fork`), `serve`. Global option `--world module:attr` on every subcommand except
`new` and `docs`.

```python
def find_world(explicit: str | None, start: Path = Path.cwd()) -> World:
    if explicit: module, _, attr = explicit.partition(":"); return _check(getattr(import_module(module), attr))
    root = _find_pyproject(start)                        # walk up to the first pyproject.toml
    name = tomllib.load(root/"pyproject.toml")["project"]["name"]
    package = re.sub(r"[-.]+", "_", name).lower()
    return _check(getattr(import_module(package), "world", None), package)
```

`_check` raises a `CliError` with the exact fix ("`<package>/__init__.py` must export `world = seahaven.World(...)`;
or pass `--world module:attr`"). The current directory is put on `sys.path` (`src/` too when it
exists) so an uninstalled world still resolves; the docs recommend `uv sync` and an editable install.

Exit codes: 0 success; 1 findings or a user error (message on stderr, no traceback); 2 argparse
usage errors. Every message is one line, plain text, and names the fix.

## 2. `seahaven new <name> [--dir <path>] [--hub]`

Renders `cli/templates/` with `string.Template` (no Jinja) into `<dir>/<name>/`, where the package
is `re.sub(r"[-.]+", "_", name).lower()`, and stops. Files:

```
pyproject.toml           # [project] name, requires-python >=3.14, dependencies = ["seahaven~=<major.minor>"],
                         #   [project.optional-dependencies] serve = ["seahaven[serve]"];
                         #   [build-system] uv_build, with [tool.uv.build-backend] module-name = <pkg>
README.md                # "# <Name>\n\nA Seahaven world.\n" plus the section headings the docs ask for
AGENTS.md                # the evergreen text plus a "## About this world" stub
src/<pkg>/__init__.py    # from .world import world; from . import tools, middleware  (explicit imports of each module)
src/<pkg>/world.py       # world = seahaven.World(name, version="0.1.0", schema=seahaven.sql_files(__package__, "schema"),
                         #   description="A Seahaven world.")
src/<pkg>/errors.py      # NotFound, InvalidInput (with from_violations), Internal: seahaven.ToolError subclasses
src/<pkg>/openenv_app.py # app = seahaven.openenv.app(world)
src/<pkg>/schema/001_items.sql        # one STRICT table `items(id TEXT PK, name TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL)`
src/<pkg>/tools/__init__.py, tools/items.py      # get_item and create_item, using ctx.ids.uuid() and ctx.clock.iso()
src/<pkg>/middleware/__init__.py, middleware/error_handler.py   # architecture §6
fixtures_src/generate.py # the stub every fixture is generated by; committed
tests/test_items.py      # @pytest.mark.seahaven(fixture=None, now="2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"): create then get,
                         #   and ids are deterministic for seed=1
tests/test_fixtures.py   # the recipe above, run: `build("empty", world=copy.copy(world))` into a tmp
                         #   directory, and `build`'s default world is this package's
fixtures/.gitkeep        # empty; the world's first fixture is frozen by its author
.gitignore               # .venv, __pycache__, work directories
```

`--hub` adds `openenv.yaml`, a root `Dockerfile` (installing `.[serve]`), a root `__init__.py`,
`client.py` and `models.py` (`components/openenv.md` §6), for a world that publishes to a hub.

Nothing is imported and no fixture is built: `new` renders templates and stops. The scaffolded test
runs against a blank instance at a fixed `now`, so a fresh scaffold passes `pytest` and
`seahaven check` with no fixture on disk. Prints the next steps (`cd`, `uv sync`, `uv run pytest`,
`uv run seahaven check`). Refuses an existing directory.

*Corrected 2026-09-13 — the file list gained `tests/test_fixtures.py`, which the scaffold now ships
because `fixtures_src/generate.py`'s `build`/`_package_world` were otherwise rendered and never run:
a `$package` substitution slip in the one line naming the package would have shipped unnoticed. The
count of files is the only thing that moved; see `components/world_and_dispatch.md` §1.1.1 for the
`world=` seam it builds through, and `BACKLOG.md` B19.*

*Corrected 2026-09-13 — the `world.py` line gained `description="A Seahaven world."`, which the
template now renders. `World` gained the argument (`components/world_and_dispatch.md` §1.1) and it
is the only thing that sets the OpenEnv one-line description, replacing the derivation of that line
from the README that `components/openenv.md` §2 specified and no longer does. A scaffold that said
nothing would publish the fallback `Seahaven world <name>`, so the template ships a placeholder
sentence with a comment telling its author to replace it. No file is added or removed by this.*

*Corrected 2026-09-13 — the `pyproject.toml` line named hatchling as the scaffold's build backend.
It is `uv_build` now, in the scaffold and in all three of this repository's own packages: hatchling
was a placeholder from the name reservation and this is a uv project (`BACKLOG.md` B24). The
scaffold also carries `[tool.uv.build-backend] module-name`, because the package this section
derives as `re.sub(r"[-.]+", "_", name).lower()` is not always the module uv derives from the
distribution name -- a name with a run of underscores diverges, and the backend would then refuse to
find the module. Nothing about the rendered file list changes.*

## 3. `seahaven check`

Runs every lint, prints findings sorted by code then path, exits 1 if any finding has severity
`error`. Findings: `Finding(code, severity: "error" | "warning", path, line, message, fix)`, printed as
`SH101 error src/pkg/schema/001.sql:12  table 'issues' is not STRICT  fix: append STRICT to the CREATE TABLE`.

Rules (each with a test fixture pair):

| Code | Sev | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| SH101 | error | table not `STRICT` | `lint/ddl.py` over an in-memory build; line found by searching the DDL text for the `CREATE TABLE <name>` |
| SH102 | error | table without an explicit primary key | ddl |
| SH103 | error | wall-clock expression in DDL (`CURRENT_*`, `'now'` time value) in any schema object | ddl, regex over `sqlite_master.sql` |
| SH104 | error | DDL fails to execute | ddl (SQLite's message) |
| SH201 | warning | wall-clock call in world code (`datetime.now`, `datetime.utcnow`, `date.today`, `time.time`, `time.monotonic`, `time.perf_counter`) outside `middleware/` | `lint/code.py`, `ast` walk of every module under the package |
| SH203 | warning | `random` module use (`import random`, `random.` calls) or `uuid.uuid4()`/`uuid1()` in world code; `ctx.ids.random` and `ctx.ids.uuid()` replay | code |
| SH205 | warning | tool with an empty description | code, via the registered `World` |
| SH301 | error | a module under `tools/` or `middleware/` not imported after importing the package | `lint/coverage.py`: `pkgutil.walk_packages` versus `sys.modules` |
| SH401 | error | fixture sidecar malformed: pydantic errors listed, including a `format_version` that is not `1` | `lint/fixtures.py` |
| SH402 | error | `file_sha256` mismatch | fixtures |
| SH403 | error | `schema_hash` does not match the world | fixtures; fix: "regenerate with `seahaven fixture ...`" |
| SH404 | error | `now` missing or not canonical | fixtures |
| SH405 | error | a fixture's state file has `-wal`/`-shm` companions[^sh405] | fixtures |
| SH501 | error | package does not export a `World` named `world` | `cli.find_world` |

SH103's hazard is the output format, not the clock: an instance's overrides already make a DDL
default read the frozen instant, but a timestamp the engine writes is not the canonical text every
other door uses, and one format across every door is the rule. The fix names `ctx.clock.iso()`.

The gaps in the numbering are deliberate: retired codes are not reused.

[^sh405]: *Corrected 2026-09-13 — SH405 read "state file not read-only or has `-wal`/`-shm`
companions"; the mode half is **dropped**, by the maintainer's decision, and this rule is now the
journal companions alone. Measured in Phase 5 and again in Phase 7 (departure 2), whose plan has the
reproduction; `seahaven/lint/fixtures.py` has implemented only this half since. Closes `BACKLOG.md`
B9.* Git records only the executable bit, so a committed fixture — which is every fixture worth
linting — comes out of any clone at `0644`, and the mode check errored on a file that is
byte-for-byte the one that was frozen: the rule fired on ProjectTracker's own untouched `empty` on
a fresh checkout. What the seal guards against is the file *changing*, and the sidecar's
`file_sha256` (SH402) and `schema_hash` (SH403) already prove the bytes, over hashes version
control does preserve. **`freeze` still does `chmod 0o444`, and that is unchanged**: sealing the
file is what stops a live instance writing a fixture in place, and dropping the check is not
permission to stop sealing. The mode is simply not something `check` can ask about.

`check` imports the world package to run SH205, SH301 and SH501; an import error is reported as
SH501 with the traceback's last line. A `SeahavenError` raised while the `World` is constructed is
caught and reported as SH104 (DDL that does not execute) or SH501 with the exception's message,
never as a traceback line.

## 4. `seahaven docs`

Prints `importlib.resources.files("seahaven") / "docs"` and exits 0. The whole output is the path,
so it composes (`cat "$(seahaven docs)/index.md"`). It is what `AGENTS.md` tells an authoring agent
to run.

## 5. `seahaven fixture`

```
seahaven fixture list                                     # id, parent, now, description (one line each)
seahaven fixture freeze <id> --run module:function --description "..." [--now <ts>]
seahaven fixture fork <parent> <id> --run module:function --description "..."
```

`freeze`: `world.instance(None, now=...)` (wall clock when omitted), import and call
`function(inst)`, `inst.freeze(id, description)`, destroy. `fork`: the same from `parent`. The
callable is the fixture's generator, written by the author (a script that uses `inst.bulk()` and the
world's tools); the CLI adds nothing to it. Prints the sidecar on success. Failure inside the
callable destroys the instance and leaves no fixture directory.

## 6. `seahaven serve`

`components/openenv.md` §4.

  passes with zero findings; `pytest` on it passes (subprocess with the current interpreter); the
  scaffold contains no `fixtures/<id>/` directory; `--hub` adds the five
  hub files and nothing else; refuses an existing directory; package name normalisation
  (`my-world` → `my_world`).
- `test_lint_ddl.py`, `test_lint_code.py`, `test_lint_coverage.py`, `test_lint_fixtures.py`: one
  positive and one negative case per code, using small worlds under `tests/worlds/`; SH201 does not
  fire inside `middleware/`; SH301 fires for a module that exists but is not imported.
- `test_cli_check.py`: output format, ordering, exit codes; DDL that does not execute is reported as
  SH104 with SQLite's message and no traceback.
- `test_cli_docs.py`: the printed path exists and holds `index.md`.
- `test_cli_fixture.py`: `freeze` and `fork` round trip on the scaffold; a generator that raises
  leaves nothing behind; `list` output.
- `test_find_world.py`: `--world` override; discovery from a subdirectory; missing `world`
  attribute message.
